✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Very nice, and always fun to count coins :D 
The Goal is very clear, the test cases are complete. Good work! 

Just a small quick note regarding:
 
    D = list(str(ar/100).split(“.”))
    if len(D[-1]) < 2:
        print(str(ar/100)+“0”)
    else:
        print(ar/100)

which can be rewritten as:

   print(f“{ar / 100:.2f}”)

Thanks to Python! :)

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: This problem is very interesting.

General
* For the time being, please switch the state of your contribution to WIP and address the issues below.

Goal
* Please change "fewer" to "fewest" (twice).

* In the last sentence, please remove the stray quotation mark, and format "No coin to give back." as a {{constant}}.

* Please add:
Assume there is an unlimited supply of each coin denomination.

Input
* All inputs except for [[n]] are floats instead of integers.

* "Line 1" appears twice.

* Please change "given" to "paid by the customer".

* Please change "nomber" to "number".

* Please change "coinsyou" to "coins you".

* Please change "each coin" to "a coin denomination, given in descending order".

Output
* Please specify the number of decimal places to show in Line 1.

* Please add "of" after "detail".

* Please remove "(one line per type of piece ! used only !)".

* Please change "ascending" to "descending".

* Please add ", one line per coin denomination used." after "order".

* Please specify the output format for each line of coin denomination used, including the exact wording and the number of decimal places to show.

* Please mention the alternative output {{No coin to give back.}}

Constraints
* Please add:
It is always possible to make the exact change using the available coin denominations.

* Please change "0,01" to "0.01".

Cases
* Please remove the trailing newlines from the output for:
  • Simple change 1 (Test 1)
  • Simple change 2 (Validator 1)
  • Bigger change 1 (Test 2)
  • Precise change 1 (Test 4)
  • Precise change 2.1 (Validator 4)

* Please split Simple change 1 and Simple change 2 into separate pairs of cases, as they represent different scenarios.

* Too many output lines start with "1 coin". Please revise the inputs so that substantially more denominations requires quantities greater than 1.

Thanks.

Thank you very much for this comment.
I'm sorry for all the english faults.
Thank you for helping me to make my puzzle better.

Thank you for aproving my contribution,
But I have a question, should I replace the whole extract and replace it by your line or I should do it in an other way,
Because, when I replace  
D = list(str(ar/100).split(“.”))
    if len(D[-1]) < 2:
        print(str(ar/100)+“0”)
    else:
        print(ar/100)
by print(f“{ar / 100:.2f}”),
the program stop working. Some cases became wrong and I can't submit it.

No worries! I've reviewed the updated version:

Input
* Please change "An float" to "A float" (3 times).

Output
* Line 1: Please change "decimal" to "decimal place". Also, some cases currently show 2 decimal places, so the formatting rule is unclear. I think it would be simpler to standardise the output to always require 2 decimal places (and update your solution accordingly).

* Please remove the quotation marks around "A coin(s) of value$", and change the text to:
[[A]] {{coin}}({{s}}) of [[value]]{{$}}

* Please format "A" (in "where A") as a [[variable]].

* Please mention that the plural form is used when [[A]] is greater than 1.

* Please add "of [[value]]" after "order".

* Please specify the number of decimal places to show for each [[value]].

* Please change "this line contains" to "output just <<one line>>".

Cases
* Very precise change 1 (Test 7): Please change [[g]] to 152.01 so that the case includes a floating point issue similar to Very big change 2 (Validator 8). This helps verify that the players handle such cases in their code correctly.

Thanks.

Thank you again for your feedback.
I've modified all the things you've found. It's very helpfull for me so if you've other remarks to do, I'll agree to learn about.
Thank you

Oh no, sorry, I've forgotten.
Now it's done

But I've a problem with one of your points :
you advised me to modify all the outputs to have 2 decimal places on each, but it didn(t work when I try to submit the modifications. it says " that doesn't match the answer from the solution provided, 1.5 "
for the exemple of the first test.
( sorry for the traduction if it's isn't said in that way in the inglish version of codingame)

After you've updated your code to always show 2 decimal places in Line 1, you have to update the cases too in order for the solution and the answer to match, e.g. change 35.0 to 35.00 in Simple change 3 (Test 2).

Output
* Add a line break before "where".

* Please format "one line" in <<bold>>.

* The current rule on the output format of [[value]] is incorrect and ambiguous:

• The first condition ([[value]] > 0) covers all positive values, so the next two conditions can never apply.
• The second condition is impossible ([[value]] is smaller than 0 while greater than or equal to 0.1).

I suggest rewording it as follows:
####################
• If [[value]] is an integer, show it without any decimal places.
• Otherwise, show [[value]] with the minimum number of decimal places required, without trailing zeros.
####################

Thanks.

Thank you again, all the modifications are done. And it work for the 2 decimal places.

No worries. The contribution looks ok now. Thank you.
